subject: Post-call: throughput, streaming needs, and residency hard stops
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@fastpay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-14T15:12:00Z
Subject: Post-demo recap & clarifying perf targets

Hi Emma — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and a few clarifying items so we can size a clean technical deep-dive: 

Summary from call:
- Goal: embed a conversational payments assistant across web and mobile checkout flows.
- Expected steady-state traffic: ~120 RPS global, with 10x peak bursts around marketing events.
- Preferred model profile: lower-latency generator for short responses (avg payload ~80 tokens).

Clarifying asks (please confirm):
1) Latency targets (p95): US <= 180 ms, EU <= 220 ms, APAC <= 360 ms — are these acceptable hard SLOs or guidance?
2) Concurrency/throughput: you mentioned 1k concurrent sessions during peak windows — is that simultaneous open sessions or sustained RPS?
3) Streaming: do you require partial token streaming (SSE/WebSocket) for progressive UX, or are chunked, non-streamed responses acceptable?
4) Data residency: you indicated EU-customer data must remain in EU for compliance. Are there any additional region-specific retention or export controls?

Attached: redwood_postdemo_checklist.pdf (post-call checklist we referenced).

Proposed next steps:
- Karthik to run a quick infra/latency feasibility check once we confirm payload size and concurrency pattern.
- Technical deep-dive (30–45m) next week to pin routing, fallback tiers, and cost estimates.

If you can reply with the three short items above (SLO confirm, concurrency semantics, streaming preference) we’ll draft a mutual action plan.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Attachment: redwood_postdemo_checklist.pdf (pdf)

From: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@fastpay.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: FastPay Security Team <security@fastpay.com>
Date: 2027-02-14T18:41:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & clarifying perf targets

Thanks Soojin — great session. Answers inline below.

On 14 Feb 2027, Soojin Lee wrote:
> 1) Latency targets (p95): US <= 180 ms, EU <= 220 ms, APAC <= 360 ms — are these acceptable hard SLOs or guidance?

Those are our goals, ideally hard SLOs for the checkout flow. We can tolerate slightly higher p99 during traffic spikes but want p95 to be consistent.

> 2) Concurrency/throughput: you mentioned 1k concurrent sessions during peak windows — is that simultaneous open sessions or sustained RPS?

Clarification: 1k concurrent *open sessions* (users with active websocket sessions). Sustained RPS during peak is closer to 800–1,200 RPS for short bursts (~10–15 minutes), then back to baseline ~120 RPS.

> 3) Streaming: do you require partial token streaming (SSE/WebSocket) for progressive UX, or are chunked, non-streamed responses acceptable?

We prefer streaming for mobile to improve perceived latency — SSE is what our frontend uses today. If Redwood supports chunked streaming with guaranteed ordering, that's fine too.

> 4) Data residency: you indicated EU-customer data must remain in EU for compliance. Are there any additional region-specific retention or export controls?

Yes — any PII tied to EU customers must stay in EU. Retention policy: 30 days for full request logs, 365 days for aggregated metrics. We will send a spreadsheet with the formal constraints (attached).

Attaching: fastpay_residency_requirements.xlsx

—Emma
Emma Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering, FastPay
emma.johnson@fastpay.com
Attachment: fastpay_residency_requirements.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@fastpay.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-15T02:07:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & clarifying perf targets

Emma — thanks for the details. A few technical notes and items I need from you to size infra and routing: 

1) Payload & token expectations:
- Average request size you mentioned ~80 tokens. Please confirm worst-case prompt + context size (tokens) and whether you will include conversation history on every request or use a partial K/V cache on the client.

2) Streaming semantics:
- We support SSE and chunked streaming; SSE is fine. For best p95 we recommend enabling prefix cache for repeated prompts and short-circuiting to smaller model variants for highly templated replies.

3) Regional routing & residency:
- For EU residency, we can host inference in EU-only clusters with a private control plane. We need to confirm whether control plane metadata is allowed to cross regions (we can restrict to EU). Also confirm whether audit logs must be stored in-region.

4) Autoscaling cadence and burst windows:
- To handle 10–15 minute 10x bursts we suggest a hybrid approach: reserved baseline capacity in each region + fast burst pool. Please share typical burst schedule (time of day/week) so we can advise warm pool size without excessive cost.

5) Acceptance criteria for SLOs:
- p95 latency target requires: (a) <200 ms model inference in-region at 1–2 concurrent tokens/loop, (b) 50–100 ms network budget. We'll create a small benchmark matrix once you confirm token sizes.

Next actions we’ll take after you confirm the items above:
- Run an initial sizing and cost estimate for Dedicated vs Private (EU-only) options.
- Prepare a short test harness for you (SSE + sample payload) to validate p95 numbers in your staging environment.

Ben — can you prepare a rough pricing delta for Dedicated baseline + burst pool per region (US/EU/APAC) and a note on SLA deviations during cross-region fallbacks?

Thanks,
Karthik
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
Attachment: none

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@fastpay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-15T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & clarifying perf targets

Emma — perfect, this gives us what we need to move forward. Quick commitments and next steps: 

Agreed points:
- Target p95: US 180 ms / EU 220 ms / APAC 360 ms (EU must be in-region for EU customers).
- Streaming: SSE preferred; Redwood will supply an SSE test harness.
- Concurrency: 1k concurrent websockets + burst RPS up to 1.2k for 10–15 minutes.
- Retention: Redwood will mirror in-region retention controls; we’ll confirm exact audit log placement in the next doc.

Next steps (owner, ETA):
- FastPay: confirm worst-case token size and whether conversation history is sent each request (Emma) — ETA: 2027-02-17
- Redwood Eng: sizing + benchmark matrix (Karthik) — ETA: 2027-02-18
- Redwood Sales/Ops: provisional pricing for Dedicated (region-by-region) + burst pool (Ben) — ETA: 2027-02-18
- Schedule technical deep-dive: proposed slot Tue 2027-02-22 16:00 UTC (calendar link) — confirm availability

Deliverables we will share when done: sizing doc, cost delta (Dedicated vs Private EU-only), and an SSE test harness with sample payloads.

Thanks — I’ll hold the calendar invite once you confirm availability.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Attachment: redwood_postdemo_checklist.pdf (pdf)
